documents.title: DH Form DD.APP.1.1 – Policies and Procedures (COMAR 10.22.02.10)
documents.issuer: Maryland Department of Health / Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA)
documents.version: 02/18. This is the version the owner supplied. The copy on the DDA website is also marked 02/18, and I found no newer one.
documents.how_used: This is the checklist the reviewer uses. For each policy item the provider marks Present Yes, No or N/A, and marks whether the policy was modified since the last OHCQ survey. The provider attaches its policies and procedures document. The provider must explain every item marked 'No' and give a plan to bring the agency into compliance. The item list below follows the form's own numbering and wording.

documents.title: COMAR 10.22.02.10 Policies and Procedures
documents.issuer: Maryland Division of State Documents / Library of Maryland Regulations (MDH/DDA regulation)
documents.how_used: This is the regulation text behind the form. I used it only to list the sub-items (a)–(g), (a)–(c) and (a)–(b) that the form's B(1), B(3) and B(5) refer to without spelling out.

required_items.text: Each individual's health and safety needs, as identified in the IP, are being met
Individuals' fundamental rights are ensured, in accordance with Health-General Article, §7-1002, Annotated Code of Maryland
Services provided in a manner that promotes individual choice and the exercise of individual rights
Confidentiality for each individual as per Health-General Article, §7-1010, Annotated Code of Maryland
Implementation of a grievance process
required_items.cite: DH Form DD.APP.1.1 p.1; COMAR 10.22.02.10A(5) (the regulation adds: with safeguards which protect against retaliatory actions for the filing of any grievance)

required_items.text: Services are provided without discrimination
All incidents are reported and investigated in accordance with DDA's Policy on Reportable Incidents and Investigations (PORI, revised 10/1/2007)
Medications administered in accordance with MATP
Compliance with COMAR 10.27.11 (Nursing delegation)
Any individual whose behaviors require intervention receive the safeguards required by regulation

In order for an individual to be required to pay for property damage caused by his/her actions, the IP shows evidence that the individual has a history of destructive behaviors that have been documented in the behavior plan (BP)
In order for an individual to be required to pay for property damage caused by his/her actions, the IP shows evidence that the individual has a BP that addresses the destructive behavior
In order for an individual to be required to pay for property damage caused by his/her actions, the IP shows evidence that the individual has the ability to pay for damages

In order for an individual to be required to pay for property damage caused by his/her actions, the IP shows evidence that the licensee's standing committee has reviewed and approved the damage payment
In order for an individual to be required to pay for property damage caused by his/her actions, the IP shows evidence that the licensee has reported the approval to the Regional Director
Compliance with H-G Article §5-605, Annotated Code of Maryland: Surrogate Decision Making
No financial or personal conflict of interest - members of governing body, staff, care providers, volunteers, standing committee
Fiscal affairs of Licensee conducted in accordance with generally accepted accounting practices
Adequate protection for finances and property of individuals, including a system to ensure funds are used appropriately for the individual's needs and preferences
Adequate protection for finances and property of individuals, including a system to keep personal funds separate from Licensee funds and the timely transfer of funds when an individual leaves
Adequate protection for finances and property of individuals, including an individual's timely access to funds
Adequate protection for finances and property of individuals, including an accounting of the individual's funds, on request
Adequate protection for finances and property of individuals, including accrual of interest, if interest bearing account
State/Federal safety precautions, infection control and standard precautions implemented
Disaster/emergency plans in place with adequate drills
Individuals do not perform duties of paid staff
Individual only performs household duties as shared by the household, as activity documented in IP, or remunerated as part of a training program
Residential service providers operating ALUs and/or GHs develop an emergency plan for all types of emergencies that includes: procedures to be followed before, during and after for (a) through (g)
The evacuation, transportation, or 72 hour shelter-in-place of individuals and staff served
required_items.cite: COMAR 10.22.02.10B(1)(a), sub-item of form item B(1)

required_items.text: Holding an annual practice drill coordinated with local emergency planners for sheltering in place or evacuating
Preparing an after action report and improvement plan after drills that evaluates the plan and takes corrective actions
Ensuring that individuals served and staff have identification with current health, contact, and other important information that is immediately accessible in the event of evacuation
The role of the resident, family member, or legal representative in the event of evacuation
Arranging for medical needs and other accommodations for individuals served and staff at alternative facilities or shelters
Establishing a communication protocol among all appropriate parties that includes redundant communication means
Residential service providers operating ALUs and/or GHs develop an emergency plan for all types of emergencies that includes: notifications to families, staff, DDA

Residential service providers operating ALUs and/or GHs develop an emergency plan for all types of emergencies that includes: staff coverage, organization, and assignment of responsibilities including (a) through (c)
Planning staff coverage needs for ongoing shelter in place or evacuations
required_items.cite: COMAR 10.22.02.10B(3)(a), sub-item of form item B(3)

required_items.text: Identifying staff members available to report for work or remain during extended periods
Establishing staff notification and recall contingency plans and procedures
Residential service providers operating ALUs and/or GHs develop an emergency plan for all types of emergencies that includes: continuity of operations
Residential service providers operating ALUs and/or GHs develop an emergency plan for all types of emergencies that includes: procedures for back-up records (a) and (b)
Backup and electronically store off-site, appropriate records and data of consumers and staff and facility documents, for access under emergency conditions
required_items.cite: COMAR 10.22.02.10B(5)(a), sub-item of form item B(5)

required_items.text: Ensure access to an electronic copy of the emergency plans when requested by local, State, or federal emergency management organizations
Residential service providers operating ALUs and/or GHs develop an emergency plan for all types of emergencies that includes: provisions to share plans with local emergency management organizations
Residential service providers operating ALUs and/or GHs develop an emergency plan for all types of emergencies that includes: executive summary of procedure provided to family member upon request
Ensure that all staff, care providers, consultants and volunteers are aware of policies and implement each policy as adopted
Provide sufficient information about the grievance process to individuals served, and/or their proponents, to enable individual to effectively use process

Explanation of all items checked 'No', with a compliance plan

notes: The reviewer works from the two-page DH Form DD.APP.1.1 (02/18) checklist. The provider submits it together with a written policies and procedures document. For each item, the provider marks Present Yes, No or N/A, and marks whether the policy was modified since the last OHCQ survey. Every item marked 'No' needs an explanation and a compliance plan in the box at the end of the form. The safest way to organize the manual is to follow the form's numbering (A(1)–A(19), B(1)–B(7), C, D, then Nursing). Put the item ID on the policy that satisfies it, so the reviewer can match each box to a page. The form has no numbers for the seven Nursing items. I labeled them Nursing-1 to Nursing-7 in the order the form lists them. These seven items cite specific Medication Training and Technical Procedures (MTTP) sections, so the medication policies should reference those sections. The DDA Qualified Provider Application (Provider Application 9.19.25) says that if DDA approves the application, the policies and procedures must be submitted to OHCQ within 30 days of approval. The A(8) and A(9) wording on the form is shorter than the regulation's. A(8) says 'MATP' on the form. The regulation refers to the Administration's curriculum on medication training. COMAR 10.22.02.10 sets no separate policy about staff training. Staff training is a separate DDA checklist, 'Staff Training – DDS (COMAR 10.22.02.11C&D)', which is also marked DH Form DD.APP.1.1 (02/18). It is a training-record form, not a policy list, so I left it out of the items. The regulation text I used for sub-items is the current version on regs.maryland.gov.
